newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - Oct 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - Oct 23.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- SING TAO DAILY - Chinese dissident Wang Xizhe who arrived in the United States last week said he wanted to join the Kuomintang. His wife said she did not understand this.
-- MING PAO DAILY - Contender for Hong Kong's post-1997 leadership Tung Chee-hwa announced an his campaign manifesto.

-- Henfrey Tin, a former colleague of ex-deputy directer of the Independent Commission Against Corruption, Alex Tsui, was sentenced to five years and a half years in jail for plotting to pervert the course of justice.
-- APPLE DAILY - Former Appeal Court judge Simon Li will announce his decision to run for the chief executive post.

-- TA KUNG PAO - Chinese vice-Premier Zhu Rongji said that China had a big market for information products and was willing to strengthen cooperation with foreign investors. He also said that China received more than US$37 billion in foreign investment this year.
-- Deputy director of the New China News Agency, Zhang Junsheng, said that Hong Kong people should not interfere with China's justice system by demonstration on behalf of dissidents.

-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES - This year's overseas orders for Hong Kong-made moulds decreased by 15 percent, showing that Hong Kong factories were facing the challenge of newly developed industrial countries.
-- European countries were considering imposing anti-dumping duties on Chinese-made bags. Forty percent of Hong Kong's bag manufacturers would be affected.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST - A consultancy study showed that China's consumer market remain in the doldrums for the next few years due to a sharp rise in the proportion of household spending on basic needs.
-- Investors fled the Shenzhen stock market in droves yesterday after the China Securities Regulatory Commission banned brokerages from lending money to customers to trade stocks.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD - The managing director of Jardine Matheson, Alasdair Morrison, resigned from the board of the Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp, following his appointment to a Jardine Fleming supervisory committee.
